title: Remote ATtestation procedureS (RATS) Architecture
algorithm_class: Normative attestation architecture: attester/evidence/verifier/relying-party roles with an evidence-concept taxonomy
supported_guarantee: Strict role and evidence taxonomy (RFC 9334 Sec. 3-4): evidence is produced by the attester about itself, verified by an evaluator, and consumed as attestation results by a relying party; freshness and trustworthiness of evidence are explicitly separated from raw self-claims and bare digests.
limitations_vs_candidate: Defines who produces and verifies attestation evidence for remote attestation of equipment, not what published AI systems' claims their evidence supports: it does not enumerate tool-dispatch, provider receipt, execution-trace or semantic-consumption classes, carries no corpus coverage matrix, no coder-agreement protocol, and no counterexample witnesses - it is baseline B0, the normative taxonomy the SoK extends rather than a competitor (novelty contract F1).
mechanism_analysis: Strongest competing explanation for RQ1 (blueprint baseline B0): if the corpus's claim/evidence structure is fully described by RFC 9334 categories the extended evidence-to-claim lattice is redundant and the SoK claim is withdrawn per the falsification rule; it is therefore cited as the claim-boundary anchor that the lattice must exceed with new cases, never rebranded. It is a normative architecture document with no executable implementation to cite (any code would be a third-party toy), so the honest status is UNAVAILABLE_NOT_RUN and it defines the evidence boundary, never a runnable arm.

title: Certificate Transparency Version 2.0
algorithm_class: Certificate Transparency v2.0: Merkle Tree Hashes and append-only log with signed tree heads and inclusion proofs
supported_guarantee: Verifiable append-only logging of certificates (RFC 9162 Sec. 2): log operators append entries whose inclusion any auditor can verify against a signed tree head; monotonically growing Merkle structure makes silent removal detectable and verifiable by third parties.
limitations_vs_candidate: Provides integrity and public auditability of a log's contents, nothing about what a log entry proves beyond presence: integrity is not confidentiality, not freshness of the attested key, not provider processing, and not execution proof - exactly the evidence-boundary separation the SoK systematizes (gap register G1/G6 class); it enumerates no AI-attestation evidence classes and no claim-evidence implication lattice.
mechanism_analysis: Boundary comparator for the transparency evidence class: CT is the canonical published system where verifiable-log evidence (inclusion proof, signed tree head) is routinely over-read as stronger assurance than it delivers, so it anchors the SoK's evidence-boundary gap register (a valid inclusion proof supports presence-in-log, never processing or execution) and the threat model's insider_or_observer family; a standard has no runnable implementation to execute as an arm, so the honest status is UNAVAILABLE_NOT_RUN and it is coded into the corpus like any other published claim source.

title: Macaroons: Cookies with Contextual Caveats for Decentralized Authorization in the Cloud
algorithm_class: HMAC caveat-chain context-bound capability credentials with first-class attenuation
supported_guarantee: Unrestricted root identifier attenuated by appended contextual caveats (actor, purpose, expiry, nonce) checked by an HMAC chain; delegation without key sharing; third-party caveats; verification either accepts or rejects the whole caveat chain.
limitations_vs_candidate: Contextual caveats bind authority at token-verification time, not attestation evidence semantics: the construction says nothing about who observed an execution, what a provider receipt proves, or which claims survive transport acknowledgment - it carries no evidence-strength levels, no observation/trust axes, and no claim-evidence implication analysis, so its inclusion codes the boundary between scoped authority and attested execution (gap G4 class), not an attestation taxonomy.
mechanism_analysis: Authority-scoping comparator for the purpose_scope/replay attack families (threat model section 2): Macaroons are the strongest published capability construction for context-bound authority, so the SoK uses it to show that even caveat-bound authorization evidence says nothing about execution or semantic consumption - authority minted for a purpose does not become attestation evidence by caveat binding (gap G8 class); the NDSS paper ships no official reference implementation (the shared baseline registry pins pymacaroons only as an independent cross-check, never as the baseline), so the honest literature-ledger status is UNAVAILABLE_NOT_RUN.

title: Zanzibar: Google's Consistent, Global Authorization System
algorithm_class: Consistency-aware distributed ReBAC authorization with zookie version tokens
supported_guarantee: Bounded-staleness permission evaluation via zookies/consistency tokens; monotonic per-user snapshot reads; global tuple-change ordering; externally consistent reads after writes (Sec. 2.3-2.4).
limitations_vs_candidate: Consistency governs permission-tuple evaluation only: zookies neither attest execution nor timestamp evidence semantics, no evidence-strength classes exist on tuples, and no claim-evidence implication is defined - an authorization decision supported at read time is a different evidence class from a provider-attested receipt or an execution trace, which is precisely the boundary the SoK maps rather than a competitor to it.
mechanism_analysis: Strong evidence-class comparator for the verification-time boundary (gap G5): Zanzibar's core published lesson is that a permission is valid only relative to a checked consistency point at evaluation time, structurally echoing the SoK's mint-time versus verify-time distinction for attestation claims (revocation_timing family); it is a design paper with no official Google code release (the shared registry routes execution through OpenFGA, which is outside this SoK's literature corpus), so the honest literature-ledger status is UNAVAILABLE_NOT_RUN and its role is to code the staleness boundary that evidence-only claims lack.

title: AgentDojo: A Dynamic Environment to Evaluate Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses for LLM Agents
algorithm_class: Dynamic stateful agent-task environment for prompt-injection attack and defense evaluation over realistic tool suites
supported_guarantee: Executable task suites with adversarial injection attacks and adaptive defenses over realistic tool environments; pinned upstream revision a75aba7631d3ca5fb7ab938965c97ead2f9ff84b (verified in the shared baseline registry as agentdojo-attack-observability, ORIGINAL_UPSTREAM, tag v0.1.35 lineage, MIT).
limitations_vs_candidate: Attack-robustness benchmarking, not attestation semantics: its utility and security scores are computed by an observer colocated with the agent harness, its attack-success oracle labels instruction compliance rather than evidence validity, and it defines no attestation evidence classes, no claim-evidence lattice levels, and no coder-agreement protocol - the SoK codes what its observability categories implicitly assume (baseline B2) without running any attack campaign of its own.
mechanism_analysis: Empirical-taxonomy baseline B2 source (blueprint): AgentDojo is executable upstream and pinned at a verified revision, and the novelty contract (F3) requires its evidence/attack observability categories to be coded into the SoK corpus as published claims - the strongest competing explanation is that these benchmark categories already separate the evidence levels, and the coverage matrix must show what they implicitly assume (agent-loop observer, task-success oracle) before any evidence-boundary claim is justified; the SoK runs no attacks, so the code link records upstream availability for corpus-coding fidelity, never a benchmark run.

title: ToolEmu: Identifying the Risks of LM Agents with an LM-Emulated Sandbox
algorithm_class: LM-emulated sandbox tool execution with LM-judge risk identification and quantified riskiness
supported_guarantee: Emulates tool executions inside an LM sandbox and uses LM judges to identify and quantify risky agent outcomes across failure axes; pinned upstream revision ac4a7ab7ed8c7985d96231e214bd6b54304b7ddb (shared registry toolemu-risk-emulation, ORIGINAL_UPSTREAM, Apache-2.0, verified 2026-11-15).
limitations_vs_candidate: Emulated tool outcomes are model-generated text, not persisted side effects: the sandbox provides simulation evidence at the assembly/emulation layer only (SoK level L0/L1 semantics), its riskiness scores are judge-assigned over emulated traces, and it defines no provider-attested receipt, TEE-attested execution or committed-consumption evidence class - simulated outcomes must never be equated with executed tool calls, which is exactly the evidence boundary the lattice separates (registry relation).
mechanism_analysis: Second half of empirical baseline B2: ToolEmu is the closest published system whose entire evidence story lives below the SoK's L2 (emulation without attested execution), so the coverage matrix codes it as a corpus claim of riskiness-from-emulated-traces and the witness gallery can contrast its judge-assigned labels with the TEE-attested L3 class; upstream is pinned and runnable (verified 2026-11-15) but the SoK performs no benchmark run - coding fidelity, not execution, is what ORIGINAL_UPSTREAM records here, keeping the evidence-boundary comparison honest without any attack or evaluation campaign.

title: tau-bench: A Benchmark for Tool-Agent-User Interaction in Real-World Domains
algorithm_class: Tool-agent-user interaction benchmark scoring policy-following and final database-state correctness in multi-turn tool use
supported_guarantee: Evaluates agents on multi-turn policy-conditioned tool use where the final database state is checked against domain policy requirements and user-interaction quality is scored by an LLM judge; pinned in the shared literature registry (tauben25) as the policy-conditioned workflow benchmark.
limitations_vs_candidate: Final-state correctness is checked by the benchmark harness's own evaluator over its own database state: the observing party is inside the evaluation loop (threat model A6 position), pass/fail is a policy-outcome verdict rather than an attestation claim, and no evidence class above harness-level checking (no receipts, no execution attestation, no committed-consumption proof anchored to a persisting service) is defined - so it bounds harness-outcome evidence but cannot justify any claim above L1 in the lattice.
mechanism_analysis: Strong outcome-evidence comparator for the L4 boundary (gap G3): tau-bench is the closest published instrument for committed database-state evaluation, so the SoK codes it to show that a policy-outcome check by an in-loop evaluator is a different, weaker evidence class than a persisting service's own verifiable record; the repository itself warns its tasks may be outdated (registry relation) and the study executes no benchmark, so the honest ledger status is UNAVAILABLE_NOT_RUN - its guarantee is cited only to bound which claims harness-internal state checks can support.

title: FHIR R5 Consent, AuditEvent and Provenance resources
algorithm_class: Interoperability standard for consent, audit-event and provenance structures (Consent purposeOfUse scope binding)
supported_guarantee: Structured Consent resources bind permitted data use to declared purposes; AuditEvent records who did what when; Provenance records entity lineage and attribution (R5): together the standard vocabulary for retrospective lineage that baseline B1 maps onto the lattice.
limitations_vs_candidate: Defines structures and exchange semantics, not evidence semantics: no attestation levels, no claim-evidence implications, no evidence-strength boundary, and FHIR compliance is not assurance - a Provenance resource records lineage claims without verifying them, which is the retrospective-versus-attestation distinction the SoK draws (baseline B1 companion to the PROV-DM row).
mechanism_analysis: Strong structural comparator for the lineage-versus-attestation boundary (novelty contract F2): FHIR AuditEvent/Provenance is the deployed healthcare vocabulary a reader could mistake for attestation evidence, so the matrix codes it to show that consent-scoped lineage recording supports who-what-when attribution but not the transport-acknowledgment/provider-receipt/execution-trace distinctions; a specification has no runnable implementation to cite as a benchmark arm (FHIR reference servers are conformance servers, not the standard), so the honest status is UNAVAILABLE_NOT_RUN and the row grounds where lineage vocabulary comes from without claiming attestation from a standard.

title: Two independent human coders applying the candidate evidence-boundary taxonomy (blueprint arm B3; candidate SoK arm)
venue: CLARA 2027 ACNS blueprint (candidate arm: two human coders + third-party adjudication per TC5, synthetic-acns-2027 fixtures)
algorithm_class: Candidate: pre-registered evidence-to-claim lattice (assembly, egress, transport acknowledgment, provider-attested receipt, execution trace, semantic consumption) applied by two independent human coders with adjudication
supported_guarantee: Claimed (not yet demonstrated): pre-registered, reproducibly extracted, independently double-coded coverage of the evidence-strength lattice with mechanized counterexample witnesses marking where each claim-evidence implication fails absent explicit trust assumptions; all thresholds and observed values enter only via artifacts/venue2027/acns/<run_id>/manifest.json after ACNS-freeze.
